2028.unvetted: Cipher still not located. All 234 images of HStAD D 4, 245/1 were downloaded from digitalisate-he.arcinsys.de (3500 x 2687 px) and read on 39 sheets of six at about 500 px per spread, with crops at full size of images 51, 186 and 222: only ordinary German letter script, a numbered list of letters (186) and an arithmetic slip (222). Short cipher runs inside a line are not excluded at that scale, and the finding aid does say 'Enthät zum Teil chiffrierte Briefe'. Nothing online names which letter; web search on Sophie Eleonore and Ludwig VI found no edition or study. Needs a line-by-line read at full size or a question to HStAD; the JPEG route needs no browser.

1543.unvetted: CPL finding aid opens in Chrome (241,000 characters; curl and WebFetch get nothing) and lists item 86.40.15 only as orders 'possibly in code'; no images are online. Search found Ruggles's clear dispatch from Columbus, Miss., to Polk of the same day, 19 Feb 1864 (OR I, 32/2), which also corrects the catalogue's '[North Carolina?]', but not this order. Whether any cipher exists needs a CPL scan of Box 8, Item 86.40.15. Side note: Box 15 holds two notebooks of 172 telegrams endorsed by Ruggles, not checked for cipher.

896.unvetted: Paz, Catalogo V, p. 32, now read as a Google Books snippet in Chrome: no. 189 'Cartas (Siete) de Lope Hurtado de Mendoza ... Medina de Rioseco 29 Noviembre s.a. - Tordesillas 10 Diciembre [1520] ... Una carta ologr. y otra' (cut at the snippet edge; 'en cifra' matches this page in the volume search). Danvila, MHE 36, prints four of the seven in clear (29 Nov, 5, 6, 10 Dec) with no cipher note, and CSP Spain Supp. vols 1-2 calendars the 10 Dec one as holograph (Patronato Real, Comunidades, leg. 2, f. 101) with no word 'cipher' in its Nov-Dec 1520 sections. So the cipher letter is probably among the three unprinted, but this is not shown. The leaf was not seen: PARES catalogo/find answers 'An application error has occurred' in Chrome. Needs PARES PTR, Comunidades leg. 2 when it answers.

1353.unvetted: Chrome passes the Anubis wall on drrp.digital.utsc.utoronto.ca. The lead is wrong about images: register 5 (utsc65994) is a metadata record with child records for pp. 7, 88, 73-4 and 118-119, and those children carry typed transcriptions, no page image; pp. 118-119, the one read in full, is continuous clear Italian with no cipher note, and register 7 'Unpaginated A' is the same kind of record. Nothing online shows ciphertext, and transcriptions do not say whether the source was cipher. Series-level record with no identified cipher leaf; needs ASVe images of the registers, and no edition of the 1576-80 Capi letters was found by search.

1382.unvetted: The ANRI inventory PDF does open in Chrome (240 pp., viewer text not extractable), and the Nationaal Archief copy gives inv. 24 as 'De inhoud van de telegrammen is veelal cryptisch'. That phrase does not show code groups, and no scan exists; held at ANRI Jakarta. A search also surfaced the ANRI microfilm inventory, with Melbourne 'code en open telegrammen' at inv. 2012 and Van Mook's code telegrams at inv. 2043-2044, which are better leads for ANRI than inv. 24. Needs a reproduction from ANRI.

1452.unvetted: AGN Guia record read in Chrome: Gobernacion, vol. 85, exp. 2, 1825, 'Carta cifrada donde se habla de una expedicion a Cuba, para liberarla del dominio espanol', no image link. The cataloguer knows the content, so a decipherment or clear copy may be with it, and the leaf has not been seen. Search on the letter and Narvaez found no printing; Narvaez 2011 (Redalyc 94120769006, read) is on Michelena 1824 and does not cite this expediente. Historia Mexicana article 1751 is behind the Cloudflare check (see 1300). Needs AGN images of the expediente.

1537.unvetted: Newberry scan 052_005 opened in Chrome, with its transcription: p. 5 begins 'all O.K. Bismark J.A.B.', the end of a telegram in clear words, then 'Opr. mentioned the above to show that Geo Godding and J.A.B. understand each other in having a cipher to use in their telegrams'. So what survives here looks like cover wording, but page 4, with the rest of the telegram, is not reachable: the record has no page navigation and collection searches for 'Godding telegram', 'Pinkerton Godding telegram' and 'Pinkerton reports Aurora cipher' returned no hit on it. Web search found nothing on this cipher. Needs scan 052_004 from the Newberry.

859.unvetted: Cipher confirmed in Chrome on ORKA 2 Ms. chem. 19[3, image 150 (f. 70v): five lines in an invented angular script with a letter table on a tipped-in slip, no decipherment visible on that leaf. Verdict still blocked by the edition: Schmitz and Winkelmann, 'Ueber die alchemistischen Geheimschriften im Briefwechsel des Landgrafen Moritz', Pharmazeutische Zeitung 106 (1961) 374-378, is not online and a new search found only Moran's work, so what it deciphers is unknown. Needs that article, by interlibrary loan or a library scan.
